{{Short description|Theorem about holomorphic functions of several complex variables}}
{{Use American English|date = June 2021}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Malgrange–Zerner theorem''' (named for [[Bernard Malgrange]] and [[Martin Zerner]]) shows that a function on <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math> allowing [[holomorphic]] extension in each variable separately can be extended, under certain conditions, to a function holomorphic in all variables jointly. This theorem can be seen as a generalization of [[Bochner's tube theorem]] to functions defined on tube-like domains whose base is not an open set.

'''Theorem'''<ref name = "Epstein">{{Cite book|last=Epstein|first=Henry|title=Some analytic properties of scattering amplitudes in quantum field theory (8th Brandeis University Summer Institute in Theoretical Physics: Particle symmetries and axiomatic field theory)|year=1966|pages=1–128}}</ref><ref name="Druzkowski">{{cite journal | last=Drużkowski | first=Ludwik M. | title=A generalization of the Malgrange–Zerner theorem | journal=[[Annales Polonici Mathematici]] | volume=38 | issue=2 | date=1999-02-22 | pages=181–186 | doi=10.4064/ap-38-2-181-186 | url=https://eudml.org/doc/265534 | access-date=2021-07-01}}</ref> Let

:<math>X=\bigcup_{k=1}^n \mathbb{R}^{k-1}\times P \times \mathbb{R}^{n-k},
\text{   where   }P=\mathbb{R}+i [0,1), </math> 
and let <math>W=</math> convex hull of <math>X</math>. Let <math> f: X\to \mathbb{C}</math> be a locally bounded function such that <math>f \in  C^\infty(X) </math> and that for any fixed point <math> (x_1,\ldots, x_{k-1},x_{k+1},\ldots,x_n)\in \mathbb{R}^{n-1}</math> the function <math> f(x_1,\ldots, x_{k-1},z,x_{k+1},\ldots,x_n)</math> is holomorphic in <math> z</math> in the interior of <math> P</math> for each <math>k=1,\ldots,n</math>. Then the function <math>f</math> can be uniquely extended to a function holomorphic in the interior of <math>W</math>.

==History==
According to [[Henry Epstein]],<ref name="Epstein" /><ref name="Epstein 1963 pp. 886–893">{{cite journal | last=Epstein | first=H. | title=On the Borchers class of a free field | journal=Il Nuovo Cimento | volume=27 | issue=4 | year=1963| doi=10.1007/bf02783277 | pages=886–893| s2cid=120708058 | url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/344209/files/CM-P00056845.pdf }}</ref> this theorem was proved first by Malgrange in 1961 (unpublished), then by Zerner <ref>Zerner M. (1961), mimeographed notes of a seminar given in Marseilles</ref> (as cited in <ref name="Epstein" />), and communicated to him privately. Epstein's lectures <ref name="Epstein" /> contain the first published proof (attributed there to Broz, Epstein and Glaser). The assumption <math>f \in  C^\infty(X) </math> was later relaxed to <math>f|_{\mathbb{R}^n}\in  C^3 </math> (see Ref.[1] in <ref name="Druzkowski" />) and finally to <math>f|_{\mathbb{R}^n}\in  C </math>.<ref name="Druzkowski" />
